_about: Every workflow the UI offers. One entry = one tab.
To add a workflow: add an entry here, a service for it in docker-compose.yml
nodes: image = LoadImage of the reference, video = VHS_LoadVideo of the driving
video, output = VHS_VideoCombine of the final result, frame_cap = the node whose
default_gpu is used only when generated/services.json is absent (plain
free_after_run (default true): after every job, tell that ComfyUI to unload its
models and drop its caches, so an idle GPU holds no weights. Costs a model reload
at the start of the next job.

replace.label: Replace character
replace.blurb: Puts the character from your image into the driving video, matching pose, framing and lighting. The result is shown side by side with the original, with the original audio. A full-length clip takes roughly an hour.
replace.gallery_blurb: Examples of character replacement: the result is your reference character in the driving video's scene.

animate.label: Animate
animate.blurb: Animates the character in your image using the motion of the driving video.
animate.gallery_blurb: Examples of animation: the reference image performing the driving video's motion.

restore.label: Restore video
restore.blurb: Restores and sharpens a low-quality video (LTX 2.5). Upload a video only; no reference image is needed. The result keeps the original audio.
restore.gallery_blurb: Examples of restoration: the original video next to the restored result.

_about_gpus: How ./start.sh spreads workflows over the GPUs it finds:
fewer GPUs than workflows -> workflows share GPUs (one queue per GPU)
one GPU per workflow      -> each gets its own
more GPUs than workflows  -> the spare GPUs get extra servers, cycling through spare_gpus
(replace, animate, replace, ...), so no workflow is left behind
gpu_plan pins workflows to GPUs by hand instead, e.g. {"replace": [0, 1], "animate": [1]}.
GPUs in gpu_plan that the machine does not have are ignored.
